title: QUIZ - 09
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Combine three fractions using multiplication and division in sequence
questions.question: Evaluate: \( \frac{8}{10} \times \frac{8}{4} \div \frac{6}{4} \)
questions.explanation: Multiplication and division of fractions are performed left to right. First \(8/10 \times 8/4 = \frac{8}{5}\), then combine with the third fraction using division (multiply by the reciprocal) to get \( \frac{16}{15} \).
questions.hint: Work left to right; for division, multiply by the reciprocal of the fraction.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply two fractions and simplify the product
questions.question: Calculate: \( 1/6 \times 6/9 \)
questions.explanation: Multiply the numerators and the denominators: \((1 \times 6) / (6 \times 9) = 6/54\), which simplifies to \( \frac{1}{9} \).
questions.hint: Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together, then simplify.

questions.learningObjective: Apply fraction multiplication to scale a recipe quantity
questions.question: A recipe uses \( \frac{3}{8} \) of hours per batch. How much is needed for 2 batches?
questions.explanation: Multiply the amount per batch by the number of batches: \( \frac{3}{8} \) \(\times 2 =\) \( \frac{3}{4} \).
questions.hint: Multiply the per-batch fraction by the number of batches.

questions.learningObjective: Apply fraction multiplication to scale a recipe quantity
questions.question: A recipe uses \( \frac{3}{2} \) of liters of juice per batch. How much is needed for 2 batches?
questions.explanation: Multiply the amount per batch by the number of batches: \( \frac{3}{2} \) \(\times 2 =\) \( 3 \).
questions.hint: Multiply the per-batch fraction by the number of batches.

questions.learningObjective: Divide two fractions using the reciprocal (keep-change-flip) method
questions.question: Calculate: \( \frac{7}{5} \div \frac{1}{10} \)
questions.explanation: Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal: \(7/5 \times 10/1 = 70/5\), which simplifies to \( 14 \).
questions.hint: To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal (flip the second fraction).
